questions.stem: A client reports new crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to the left arm with diaphoresis and nausea. Which action should the nurse take first?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Administer an antacid and reassess the pain after gastrointestinal causes have been excluded at the bedside.","B":"Have the client ambulate briefly to determine whether the discomfort is reproducible with physical activity.","C":"Place the client on cardiac monitoring, obtain a 12-lead ECG promptly, and activate the acute coronary syndrome pathway.","D":"Delay diagnostic testing until a troponin result is available because ECG findings are not useful before biomarkers rise."}}
questions.rationale: This presentation is concerning for acute coronary syndrome. Immediate cardiac assessment and a prompt 12-lead ECG are central to early evaluation while the ACS pathway is activated. Antacid testing, exertion, or waiting for biomarkers can delay recognition and treatment of myocardial ischemia.
questions.source_name: ACC/AHA/ACEP/NAEMSP/SCAI — 2025 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Acute Coronary Syndromes
